title: Volume-first plan: HC and price sensitivity lab
summary: Working sheet exploring a volume-first commercial plan: phased HC hires to support Dedicated/Hosted growth, incremental reserved capacity, and the price delta required under three demand scenarios. Goal: give product + sales a simple price trigger and hiring gating framework.
assumptions: Baseline total monthly token units (1k-token units): 120,000,000 (represents ~120B tokens/month)
Current blended revenue per 1k tokens (avg across routes): $0.004
Operational cost per 1k tokens (variable infra + GPU): $0.002
Average fully-loaded annual cost per new hire: $220,000
Reserved capacity incremental fixed cost to enable 40% higher p95 throughput: $60,000/month
Hiring start date window: Jul 2026 - Dec 2026 (phased)
We assume 30% of growth traffic is tail-latency sensitive and will land on Dedicated/reserved pools requiring extra fixed capacity
scenarios: Base growth (base): volume +20% over 12 months, no price change, modest efficiency gains via kv-caching reduce variable cost per 1k to $0.0018 by Q4. Required incremental hires: 4 infra/serving, 1 SRE, 1 finance ops (6 total). Incremental monthly headcount cost: $110,000.

Price-up (price): assume +10% list price across hosted API in Oct 2026; volume sensitivity -5% (slight churn), net volume +13%. Efficiency improvements as above. Incremental monthly headcount cost same: $110,000. Revenue per 1k becomes $0.0044.

Demand shock (shock): sudden enterprise slowdown -> volume -30% compared to baseline. Need to keep Dedicated commitments and partial reserved capacity. Hiring is deferred to 2 hires (critical SRE + infra), incremental monthly headcount cost: $36,666 (annualized). Reserved capacity still needed for contracted throughput: $40,000/month incremental.
unit_economics: Baseline contribution margin = $240,000/month (50%) before fixed costs
Incremental fixed costs (6 hires + reserved): hires $110,000/month + reserved $60,000/month = $170,000/month
Net after incremental = contribution margin - incremental fixed = $70,000/month under Base growth assumptions (before taxes & non-op)
If variable cost improves to $0.0018, variable cost becomes $216,000 -> contribution margin $264,000 -> net after incremental $94,000/month
breakeven_prices: Base scenario: to cover incremental fixed $170,000 with baseline units 120,000,000 -> required delta = $170,000 / 120,000,000 = $0.001417 per 1k -> new blended price = $0.005417 (=> ~35% price increase)

Price-up scenario (+10% list): blended price = $0.0044, contribution increases by $48,000/month vs baseline. With same incremental costs ($170k) gap is $122k still to cover -> required additional delta per 1k = $122,000 / 120,000,000 = $0.001016 -> effective blended price needed = $0.005416. (similar breakpoint)

Demand-shock scenario: active units 84,000,000 (30% drop). Fixed incremental cost (hires deferred) = $36,666 + reserved $40,000 = $76,666/month. Required delta per 1k = $76,666 / 84,000,000 = $0.000912 -> blended price to break even = $0.004912.
notes: The math above is intentionally simplified (blended across product routes). Product should validate per-route elasticity (chat vs embeddings vs embeddings batch).
Model mix matters: embeddings have higher $/1k but also higher variable cost per embed job; dedicated customers carry different margin profile — consider separate per-route tables.
We haven't included churn feedback loops from price increases (market competitive risk). Sales input required on enterprise contract repricing windows.
Consider run-rate savings from quantization/compilation improvements: 10-18% GPU cost down would materially reduce required price deltas.
Concord with infra on feasibility of incremental reserved capacity being staged monthly (not all at once) — reduces upfront burn.
